title: How Long to Do 4-7-8 Breathing: 4 Cycles, About 76 Seconds

copy.cover_headline: You only need 4 rounds of 4-7-8 breathing

points.headline: One cycle takes 19 seconds
points.body: 4 in, 7 hold, 8 out. Four cycles take about 76 seconds. That's the usual starting point, at least twice a day for the first month.

points.headline: The steps
points.body: Tongue behind upper front teeth. Whoosh out through your mouth. In through your nose for 4. Hold for 7. Whoosh out for 8. Repeat for 4 cycles, sitting or lying down.

points.headline: Lightheaded? Halve the count
points.body: Stop and breathe normally first. Next time try 2-3.5-4: same ratio, half the hold, under 40 seconds for 4 cycles. A smaller, quiet inhale helps too.

points.headline: Or skip the hold entirely
points.body: 4-6 breathing: in for 4, out for 6, no hold. In a 2025 study of 84 people, 6 breaths a minute raised heart rate variability more than 4-7-8. Effects were small to medium.

points.headline: More isn't better
points.body: Weil's guidance tops out at 8 cycles (about 2.5 minutes) after a month of practice. Tingling, air hunger, or a pounding heart means stop and do fewer next time.

reel_lines: You opened the app to check one thing.
Now your jaw is tight and you feel wired.
A few slow breaths can bring you back down.
copy.instagram_caption:
You only need about 76 seconds of 4-7-8 breathing. Here's the count.

Sit or lie down. Breathe in through your nose for 4, hold for 7, whoosh out through your mouth for 8. That's 19 seconds. Do 4 cycles, then breathe normally.

If the hold makes you lightheaded, stop. Next time try 2-3.5-4: same ratio, half the time.

copy.facebook_message:
4-7-8 breathing is easier to dose than most people think. One cycle (in for 4, hold for 7, out for 8) takes 19 seconds, so the usual starting point of 4 cycles takes about 76 seconds. Twice a day is the common guidance.

If the 7-second hold leaves you lightheaded, stop and breathe normally. Next time use the faster 2-3.5-4 count, which keeps the same ratio, or try 4-6 breathing with no hold at all.

It's a handy reset when the feed has left you wired. DeRot, our upcoming iOS app, pauses your apps while you reset with a few calming breaths.

Read the full guide for the timing math and what the research does and doesn't show.
